British American Tobacco stock faces weak BAT Bangladesh earnings
sum: British American Tobacco stock traded at 55.89 euros on Lang & Schwarz at 10:41 CET on Thursday, November 5, 2026. The latest regional earnings signal came from BAT Bangladesh PLC, which reported a sharp decline in third-quarter profit.

According to The Business Standard, BAT Bangladesh reported the figures for the quarter ended September 30 on October 29. Net profit after tax fell 67.28% year on year to 99.84 crore taka from 305.04 crore taka in the same quarter of 2025.

Quarterly earnings per share declined to 1.85 taka from 5.65 taka. Net revenue from contracts with customers fell to 1,259 crore taka from 1,677.13 crore taka a year earlier. The report attributed the weaker result to lower revenue and higher operating expenses.

The deterioration extended across the first nine months of 2026. BAT Bangladesh said net profit after tax fell 28.77% to 513.02 crore taka from 720.26 crore taka in the same period of 2025. Nine-month net revenue declined to 5,090 crore taka from 5,754 crore taka, while earnings per share fell to 9.50 taka from 13.34 taka.

The company reported gross revenue of 7,328.34 crore taka for the quarter. Supplementary duty and value-added tax deductions amounted to 6,068.78 crore taka, highlighting the importance of tax and pricing conditions in the local tobacco market.

The Bangladesh figures concern a locally listed company and are not consolidated results for British American Tobacco plc. They nevertheless provide a regional operating signal for investors monitoring tobacco demand, taxation and cost pressure in South Asian markets. The reported contraction also shows how quickly local earnings can diverge from broader group expectations.

For the parent company's shares, the immediate focus remains on group-level revenue growth, new nicotine categories and capital allocation. The Bangladesh report alone does not establish a change in British American Tobacco plc's consolidated outlook or explain the movement of its stock.

Organigram-Aurora $561 million deal taps Goodmans, Torys, Stikeman Elliott, Paul Weiss
sum: Canadian cannabis deal brings together four law firms as Organigram seeks to acquire Aurora at 93% premium

Organigram Global Inc. has engaged Goodmans LLP as its legal adviser for its proposed C$561 million acquisition of Aurora Cannabis Inc., which is advised by Stikeman Elliott LLP and Paul, Weiss, Rifkind, Wharton & Garrison LLP. Torys LLP is advising Aurora’s special committee, while Osler, Hoskin & Harcourt LLP is acting as legal counsel to British American Tobacco, Organigram’s strategic shareholder.

BMO Capital Markets is serving as Organigram’s financial adviser and has provided a fairness opinion to its investment committee and board. Fort Capital Partners is advising Aurora and has provided a fairness opinion, while Origin Merchant Partners is advising Aurora’s special committee and has also provided a fairness opinion.

The proposed acquisition emerged from a strategic review undertaken by Aurora under the oversight of its independent directors’ special committee, following Curaleaf’s unsolicited takeover proposal. The committee and Aurora’s board have unanimously recommended the Organigram transaction to shareholders, describing it as the best actionable route to maximise shareholder value.

Under the arrangement agreement, Aurora shareholders can elect to receive C$7.80 in cash, 5.8626 Organigram shares, or a combination of C$3.75 in cash and 3.0431 Organigram shares for each Aurora share, subject to proration limits.
Aurora shareholders are expected to hold approximately 35% of the combined company’s economic ownership on a fully diluted basis and 42% of its voting ownership.

The combined entity aims to strengthen its position in Canada, Europe and Australia by bringing together Organigram’s recreational cannabis business and research and development capabilities with Aurora’s international medical cannabis operations and EU-GMP-certified manufacturing facilities.

Aurora Cannabis Stock Surges on Organigram Deal
sum: Aurora Cannabis Inc ACB shares are booming Tuesday after the company agreed to be acquired by Organigram Global for 7.80 Canadian dollars ($5.57) per share, a deal that tops a rival hostile offer from Curaleaf. Here’s what you should know.
- Aurora Cannabis stock is surging to new heights today. Why is ACB stock up today?

Aurora Cannabis shares are rising after Organigram agreed to buy the company for C$7.80 a share, an equity value of about C$561 million. Aurora holders pick how they get paid. They can take all cash, take only Organigram stock at 5.8626 shares for each of their own, or split the payment between C$3.75 in cash and 3.0431 Organigram shares.

The price is 93% above Aurora’s price on Aug. 10, the final complete session before Curaleaf revealed its hostile plan, and 21% above Curaleaf’s current bid, which was last amended on Oct. 6. Aurora’s board unanimously rejected that bid. It now calls the Organigram deal better for shareholders and tells them not to tender to Curaleaf.

The two Canadian cannabis companies say they would run five sites with EU-GMP certification and hold leadership positions in Canada, Europe and Australia. They also count on more than C$50 million in synergies. After closing, Aurora holders would own about 35% of the combined economics and hold 42% of the votes. Organigram CEO James Yamanaka called the deal a “defining step” for the company’s strategy.
British American Tobacco, Organigram’s cornerstone shareholder, will buy about C$187.5 million of new Organigram shares at C$1.33 to help pay the cash portion.

Two-thirds of the votes cast by Aurora shareholders must back the deal, and so must a majority of the holders outside certain insiders. Organigram shareholders also vote, and British American Tobacco’s 30% of Organigram’s votes is committed in favor even though it sits outside that count.

British American Tobacco stock faces dividend date as 2026 outlook holds
sum: British American Tobacco is heading into a scheduled dividend payment while keeping its 2026 revenue outlook unchanged. Simply Wall St reports that eligible shareholders are due to receive 0.6126 pounds per share on Friday, November 6, after an October 1 ex-dividend date and an October 2 record date.

The payment is part of BAT's quarterly distribution plan. The company declared a total interim dividend of 2.4504 pounds per ordinary share for the year ending December 31, 2026, with equal instalments scheduled across May, August, November and February, according to the dividend information carried by Simply Wall St.

BAT continues to target 2026 revenue growth of 3% to 5% at constant exchange rates, adjusted for Canada. The company expects performance toward the lower end of that range. The guidance was reaffirmed in the company's 2026 updates, including the half-year report listed on BAT's press release page.

The outlook reflects a business still balancing resilient combustible tobacco operations with investment in newer nicotine categories. BAT's half-year materials described performance as in line with expectations, while the company has continued to emphasize growth in vapour, heated products and modern oral products such as nicotine pouches.

That mix is important for investors because the long-term growth case depends increasingly on products outside traditional cigarettes. At its September Capital Markets Day, BAT set out ambitions for its Horizon 2030 strategy, while maintaining its medium-term growth algorithm. Execution in New Categories, pricing, currency movements and the pace of cigarette-volume declines remain key variables for earnings and cash generation.

British American Tobacco stock traded at 55.43 euros on Lang & Schwarz at 09:20 CET on Monday, November 2, 2026, 0.56 percent above the Xetra close of Friday, October 30. Investors can follow the real-time quote of British American Tobacco stock.
The scheduled distribution provides a near-term cash-return event, but the central valuation question remains whether New Category growth can offset pressure on the legacy portfolio.

BTI vs. PM: Which Tobacco Dividend Will Actually Survive the Industry’s Decline?
sum: Both BTI and PM fund generous dividends from a shrinking cigarette business, but one company's smoke-free pivot has already changed what its payout is built on, and that gap matters far more than the headline yield difference.

British American Tobacco (NYSE:BTI | BTI Price Prediction) or Philip Morris International (NYSE:PM): which Big Tobacco dividend should an investor planning for retirement own right now? Both fund their payouts from cigarettes in structural decline, and both are spending heavily to replace them with smoke-free products. The better pick is the company whose transition already pays the bills. On that test, Philip Morris wins, even though BAT carries the higher headline yield and cheaper valuation.

The market agrees. Philip Morris shares are up 21.91% year to date, while BAT is down 0.71%. Over 10 years on an adjusted basis, Philip Morris gained 221.75% against 67.32% for BAT. Morningstar noted today that BAT’s Capital Markets Day reaffirmed its midterm growth algorithm, but the market expects far worse.
Dividend Track Record: Philip Morris Raises Faster and Pays in Dollars

Philip Morris just lifted its quarterly dividend from $1.47 to $1.60, payable October 26, 2026, for an annualized forward rate of $6.40. That follows an 8.9% increase in 2025, and its record shows steady quarterly payments stretching back to June 2008. The trailing yield is 3.03%.

BAT declared 245.04p per share for FY2025, paid in four payments of 61.26p, a 2.0% raise. Structure matters here. BAT is a UK-based foreign private issuer whose U.S. shares trade as American depositary receipts, and it commits to dividend growth in sterling terms. The dollar check a U.S. holder receives therefore moves with the exchange rate: the quarterly payment was $0.746191 in 2021, dipped to $0.700605 in 2023 and now stands at $0.834851. Philip Morris, a U.S.-domiciled corporation, declares and pays in dollars. Winner: Philip Morris.

Philip Morris expects roughly $13.5 billion of operating cash flow in 2026, and Q2 operating cash flow rose 61% to $5.492 billion. Raised 2026 guidance calls for adjusted diluted EPS of $8.26 to $8.41, well above the $6.40 annualized dividend.

British American Tobacco stock gains as analysts stick to Moderate Buy outlook
sum: British American Tobacco p.l.c. (ISIN GB0002875804) stock was quoted around USD 57 on the New York Stock Exchange on September 14, 2026, while analysts maintained a consensus price target of USD 68.10, signaling roughly 19.1 percent upside from recent levels.

According to MarketBeat on September 14, 2026, British American Tobacco stock carries a consensus rating of Moderate Buy based on research coverage from seven analysts, with an average rating score of 2.71 on a 0-to-4 scale. The same overview shows a single consensus price target of USD 68.10, which stands about 19.1 percent above the current price of approximately USD 57.19 and represents the market's view on medium-term appreciation potential.

The MarketBeat data further indicate that the stock offers a dividend yield of 5.73 percent as of September 14, 2026, underlining its appeal for income-focused investors alongside the capital gains implied by the target price. At a share price of USD 57.22, the company’s market capitalization is reported at USD 116.15 billion on the same date, placing British American Tobacco firmly among the largest global consumer defensive groups in the tobacco and nicotine segment.

As Zacks Investment Research reported on September 14, 2026, the Zacks Consensus Estimate for British American Tobacco’s earnings per share in fiscal 2026 stands at USD 4.82 and for 2027 at USD 5.20. These estimates have remained unchanged over the preceding seven days, suggesting that analysts currently see a relatively stable earnings trajectory. The implied increase from USD 4.82 in 2026 to USD 5.20 in 2027 corresponds to EPS growth of about 7.9 percent, which in turn supports the view that the company can fund its transformation and dividend commitments from continuing cash generation in the traditional combustible business.

Zacks highlights that British American Tobacco is backed by strong pricing power and robust cash flows from its core tobacco operations, which provide room to invest in reduced-risk and newer-category products while maintaining shareholder returns.

FTSE 100 movers: Coca-Cola HBC hit by downgrade; Glencore gains
sum: London’s FTSE 100 was down 0.4% at 10,858.04 in afternoon trade on Monday.
Coca-Cola HBC fizzed lower after a downgrade to ‘neutral’ from ‘outperform’ at BNP Paribas, which cited limited further upside following the stock's strong run.
Legal & General was also weaker after Citi downgraded the shares to ‘sell’ from ‘neutral’ on valuation grounds and cut the price target to 245p from 251p as it noted the stock is up 19% year to date.

The bank said it was cutting its 2026-27 remittances by 4.5% following the first-half results. "This reflects lower pension buyout volumes underwritten at a reduced IFRS margin offset by higher operating profit from asset management driven by lower CIR, and an additional £100m per annum from asset optimisation actions," it said.
Defensive were on the back foot, with pharma giant GSK and tobacco stocks Imperial Brands and British American Tobacco all down.
On the upside, Glencore was the standout gainer on the index as Deutsche Bank, which rates the shares at ‘buy’, said it continues to see a compelling bottom-up story for the miner.

"Near-term progress on divestments should lead to higher shareholder returns; copper volumes should lift materially over the next 12-18 months (little in the share price for this); and we believe Rio merger talks could be revived at some stage, potentially once both companies have made progress on divestments," the bank said.
